text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan holds talks with Algerian Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia and confirms the U.N will send observers to supervise Algeria's June 5 legislative elections.
- Lebanon's Hizbollah party leader Sheik Fadlallah told El Ouma: "We do not want Algeria to experience what Lebanon did in the civil war."
- Algeria to open exchange stock market before the end of 1997.

- Socialist Forces Front to take part in parliamentary elections. The party leadership endorses the decision following consultations with the FFS leader Hocine Ait Ahmed who is in self-exile in Europe.
- Algerian and Egyptian foreign ministers preside over joint-committee meeting on cooperation in Cairo.
- Seven assassins of retired general Habib Khelil were killed in the western city of Oran.
- A car bomb kills four people and wounds 27 in Boumerdes, east of Algiers, on Thursday.
